title: Open restriction transports cycle-compatible homology evaluation
statement: Let X be a scheme, T,J integer cochain complexes of X-modules, n an integer, and e:H^n(Hom(T,J))->Hom(H^(-n)(T),H^0(J)) satisfying IsHomologyEvaluation [new-b2-homology-evaluation-definitions]. For opens V of X and W of V.toScheme, let F be moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor, A=F(T), K=F(J), Q=Hom(A,K) [def-pur-hom-complex], and pi its fixed (-n,0) product projection [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]. There exist a:F(H^n(Hom(T,J))) iso H^n(Q), b:F(Hom(H^(-n)(T),H^0(J))) iso Hom(H^(-n)(A),H^0(K)), g:H^n(Q)->Hom(H^(-n)(A),H^0(K)), and d:Z^n(Q)->Hom(Z^(-n)(A),Z^0(K)). They satisfy d;Hom(1,iCycles_K)=iCycles_Q;pi;Hom(iCycles_A,1), d;Hom(1,homologyPi_K)=homologyPi_Q;g;Hom(homologyPi_A,1), and F(e);b.hom=a.hom;g. There is no roof or K-injectivity assumption.

source.place: Hom complexes, differential and precomposition; Tag 08DL for the restriction comparison.

proof.text: First construct the ambient cycle pairing d0 directly. Compose the fixed degree-n product projection with the inclusions of Hom cycles and source cycles. Apply the Hom differential formula in degree (-n,1); the source-cycle differential is zero, so the evaluation is killed by the target differential. Uncurry via tensorHomEquiv, lift through the kernel defining target cycles, and curry back. This proves the inclusion identity. At each open U and local cycles phi,z, its value b satisfies exactly the premise of IsHomologyEvaluation. Apply he to obtain the homology identity at the identity slice. Restrict phi to each slice object and use naturality of local linear maps to extend this to every slice component. Sheaf and module-morphism extensionality prove the ambient homology identity.

Obtain the six restriction isomorphisms a,b,c,s,t,v and their five compatibility equations from the restriction-diagram lemma. This lemma is independent of e and of IsHomologyEvaluation and records only the canonical comparison data.

Apply the proved generic transport_cycle_pairing lemma. It defines g=a.inv;F(e);b.hom and d=c.inv;F(d0);s.hom. Rewrite d followed by target cycle inclusion using the second comparison square, F(d0;inclusion)=F(raw evaluation), then the first square and c.inv;c.hom=1. For the homology identity similarly use the third square and the ambient identity; use the fifth square for source homology and the fourth square in the form c.inv;F(P.homologyPi)=Q.homologyPi;a.inv. Associativity gives the asserted formula. Finally a.hom;a.inv=1 gives the square for F(e). The helper is proved for arbitrary categories and functors to avoid repeatedly unfolding the concrete sheaf types.

proof_origin.description: Ambient kernel lift and conversion of the local representative hypothesis are proved in Lean. Restriction comparison data are split into one strict subargument without any evaluation morphism. Generic categorical transport completes the original theorem.

theorem homologyEvaluation_restriction_comparison (X : Scheme.{u})
    (T J : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (n : ℤ)
    (e : (homComplex (R := X.sheaf) T J).homology n ⟶
      SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf) (T.homology (-n)) (J.homology 0))
    (he : IsHomologyEvaluation X T J n e) (V : X.Opens) (W : V.toScheme.Opens) :
    let A := (moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor X V W).obj T
    let K := (moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor X V W).obj J
    let Q := homComplex (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) A K
    let π := (Classical.choose
      (homComplex_projections_exists (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)))
      A K n (-n) 0 (by omega)
    ∃ a : ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
        ((homComplex (R := X.sheaf) T J).homology n)).over W ≅ Q.homology n,
      ∃ b : ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
          (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf)
            (T.homology (-n)) (J.homology 0))).over W ≅
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (A.homology (-n)) (K.homology 0),
        ∃ g : Q.homology n ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (A.homology (-n)) (K.homology 0),
          ∃ d : Q.cycles n ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
              (A.cycles (-n)) (K.cycles 0),
            d ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
                (𝟙 _) (K.iCycles 0) =
              Q.iCycles n ≫ π ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap
                (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (A.iCycles (-n)) (𝟙 _) ∧
            d ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
                (𝟙 _) (K.homologyπ 0) =
              Q.homologyπ n ≫ g ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap
                (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (A.homologyπ (-n)) (𝟙 _) ∧
            (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map e).over W) ≫ b.hom =
              a.hom ≫ g
